item.title: Scientists identify brain waves that define the limits of 'you'
item.description:
📝 Now, scientists have linked a specific set of brain waves in a certain part of the brain to a sense of body ownership. Those with faster alpha waves appeared to rule out fake hands even with a tiny gap in taps, while those with slower waves were more likely to feel the fake hand as their own, even if the taps were farther apart. And sure enough, this seemed to correlate with how real a fake hand felt.
🔗 Read more: https://www.sciencealert.com/scientists-identify-brain-waves-that-define-the-limits-of-you

item.title: The '3.5% rule': How a small minority can change the world (2019)
item.description:

They primarily considered attempts to bring about regime change. Strength in numbersOverall, nonviolent campaigns were twice as likely to succeed as violent campaigns: they led to political change 53%.

item.title: The behavioral cost of personalized pricing
item.description:
📝 With that knowledge, I find myself abandoning carts even when the price was fine before, on the off chance that a discount materializes. In December 2025, Groundwork Collective found that Instacart was charging individualized prices. Some people paid 23% more for the exact same item, from the exact same store, at the exact same time.
🔗 Read more: https://digitalseams.com/blog/the-behavioral-cost-of-personalized-pricing
